description: 24 camera comparisons: 3 distances ? 4 layouts ? 2 encounter densities. Percentages are prompt targets; direct observations distinguish actual results. Camera recommendation is owner input only.
common: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: arena camera comparison, not a production sprite. Original Roman-era elemental-mage prison arena. Hand-drawn digital, flat fresco colours, edge tesserae, quiet matte ground. Composition and small character scale take priority over facial detail. No text, UI, lettering, numbers, logos, borrowed designs, photographic textures, 3D or cinematic foreground characters.

items.prompt: CAMERA: distant high overhead orthographic gameplay view, 55 degrees above the ground, looking steeply down. Each human head-to-sole silhouette occupies ONLY 5 percent of total image height (about 36 pixels in a 720-pixel-high image). Tiny figures, huge open ground; all humans equally small, no foreground hero. The camera sees a local patch of an arena three screens wide. Do not fit the complete arena into the image. LAYOUT: An enormous open sand-and-lime oval. Only a fragment of its distant boundary at the very top; floor continues outside the other three edges. No enclosing postcard frame. ENCOUNTER: one mineral-blue water mage and four widely separated opponents. Player near centre, enemies around the middle thirds; every silhouette separated by at least three figure heights of clear ground. A small outgoing blue water needle, one incoming vermilion fire projectile and a clearly visible pale-turquoise FORWARD 140-degree crescent absorb in front of the player, rear completely open. Two clearly distinct hollow ground danger circles with short radial ticks, each wider than two figures. Absorb and warnings are larger than figures but never dominate the whole arena. Threat silhouettes include a net fighter, bronze shield bearer, ember caster and coal hound. Even the busy scene retains broad empty movement lanes. No interface or lettering.
